observation.description: With offlineQueue: true, an offline mutate on the Expo carrier surfaces the raw transport error ("fetch failed: UnexpectedException: Could not connect to the server. (at ExpoModulesCore/Promise.swift:56)", name 'Error') instead of queueing. The client's connectivity classification (index.mjs isConnectivityFailureError) requires `error instanceof TypeError`; Expo's fetch rejects connection failures with a plain Error, so the M2 queue path can never engage on this carrier. Node control with identical options and an explicit createMemoryRqsResumeStore against the same stopped server queues {queued:true, sequence:1} - the non-engagement is the error-class check, not the store.

competitorOutcome.description: Firestore's RN SDK queues writes offline and settles them on reconnect as a core documented behavior (frozen Diary 0027 evidenced the same shape on web).

mustNotRegress: The fail-closed half of the classification: anything the server answered (refusals, conflicts, rejections) must still NEVER queue.
smallestCoherentFix: Classify connectivity by transport-layer provenance (fetch rejection with no HTTP status, no diagnostic, no receipt) independent of the error's constructor, or normalize carrier fetch rejections in the shared transport before classification; add a packaged-closure conformance test that runs the queue path under an Expo-fetch-shaped Error.
acceptanceWitness: On an Expo simulator with the server stopped, an offlineQueue-enabled mutate returns {queued:true, clientMutationId, sequence} and replays exactly once after reconnect ({replayed:1, failed:0, remaining:0}).
